title: Add end-to-end integration tests for route-level quantization profiles
author: Leila Farouk
release_notes: Internal: Adds end-to-end integration coverage for quantization profile resolution + routing fallback + runtime application signals.
description:
Motivation
We’ve landed the core building blocks for the Quantization Profile Library v1 (route config field, policy compatibility guardrails, runtime load/apply). Before we start beta canaries, we need an end-to-end test suite that validates the full request path:
- Control plane route config resolution (explicit profile ref vs default)
- Policy engine compatibility checks and deterministic fallback to baseline
- Routing propagation of the resolved decision to the runtime
- Runtime application signaling (applied vs fallback vs disabled)

What this PR does
Adds a hermetic E2E integration test suite that spins up a minimal in-process stack (config service + policy evaluator + router + runtime test harness) and runs request-level assertions against the resolved quantization outcome.

Covered scenarios
1) Explicit profile ref, compatible
- Route config sets quantization_profile_ref = "qpl://llama-3-8b-instruct/int8-kv/v1"
- Policy evaluation returns resolved_profile_id and outcome=APPLIED
- Runtime receives resolved profile and reports quant_profile_resolution_outcome=applied

2) Explicit profile ref, incompatible -> fallback
- Profile constrained to GPU class "H100" but request targets "L4" pool
- Policy evaluation returns outcome=FALLBACK_BASELINE with reason=INCOMPATIBLE_HARDWARE
- Router passes baseline mode to runtime (no profile artifact fetch)
- Runtime reports quant_profile_resolution_outcome=fallback

3) Feature off (default behavior)
- quantization_profile_ref unset (or set to "default")
- Outcome=DISABLED, runtime remains baseline

4) Determinism / cache
- Same route + model + region evaluated repeatedly produces identical resolution
- Verifies policy evaluator cache key includes (route_id, model_id, region, deployment_tier, gpu_class)

5) Kill-switch honored
- With global kill-switch enabled, explicit profile refs are ignored
- Outcome=DISABLED_KILL_SWITCH

Implementation notes
- Uses a small “runtime test harness” that implements the runtime-side contract used by routing (resolved profile id + mode) and emits the same counters the production runtime does.
- Avoids GPU runners by not executing real kernels; the runtime harness validates that the resolved profile id is applied to the request context and that the artifact fetch path is invoked only when outcome=APPLIED.
- Adds golden JSON fixtures for:
  - sample profiles (compatible + incompatible)
  - route config payloads
  - policy resolution responses

Test plan
- New suite runs in CI under the "integration" job.
- Locally: ./bazel test //tests/integration:quant_profiles_e2e_test (or make test-integration)

Risk
Low. Tests only; no production code paths changed. A couple of small refactors were required to make the router/runtime boundary injectable in tests (no behavior changes).

Follow-ups
- Once pr-18555 (log annotations with quant_profile_id) is everywhere, we can extend assertions to trace fields in addition to metrics.
- Consider adding a single GPU-backed smoke test in perf-canary for one model once we finalize runners.
commits: tests/integration: add stack harness for quant profile resolution
router: allow injecting runtime client for integration tests (no behavior change)
policy: expose structured fallback reason for test assertions
ci: add integration target to buildkite step
fixtures: add sample profiles + route configs for e2e cases
changed_areas: ci/buildkite pipeline definition for integration tests
files_changed_summary:
Key files
- tests/integration/quantization_profiles/quant_profiles_e2e_test.go
- tests/integration/quantization_profiles/stack_harness.go
- tests/integration/quantization_profiles/fixtures/profiles/*.json
- tests/integration/quantization_profiles/fixtures/routes/*.json
- router/runtime/runtime_client.go (constructor injection)
- policy/engine/resolution.go (expose fallback reason enum)
- ci/buildkite/pipeline.yml (add integration step)

Illustrative snippet (test assertion)
- Assert(APPLIED): expects outcome=applied and resolved_profile_id matches route ref
- Assert(FALLBACK): expects outcome=fallback and resolved_profile_id empty, with fallback_reason=INCOMPATIBLE_HARDWARE
- Assert(KILL_SWITCH): expects outcome=disabled_kill_switch even when route sets explicit ref
review_conversation:
Ethan Park (Control Plane) — Requested changes:
- “Can we assert that registry/profile metadata fetch is not called on fallback/disabled? That’s the failure mode that caused a thundering herd in earlier spikes.”
Leila Farouk — Updated:
- Added a fake registry client with call counters; tests now assert fetch_count==0 when outcome != APPLIED.

Mina Haddad (Routing) — Comment:
- “Please ensure the determinism test covers region/deployment tier as part of the cache key. We’ve had regressions where tier wasn’t included.”
Leila Farouk — Updated:
- Added a matrix test that varies (region, deployment_tier) and asserts independent cache entries.

Noah Patel (Runtime) — Comment:
- “Runtime harness should validate that we don’t attempt artifact load on fallback. Also, can we name the outcome metric exactly as prod?”
Leila Farouk — Updated:
- Matched the metric name to runtime.quant_profile.resolution_outcome and added an assertion around artifact_loader.calls.

Jordan Lee (Policy Determinism) — Requested change:
- “Fallback reason strings should be enums not free-form. Tests shouldn’t lock in text.”
Leila Farouk — Updated:
- Switched assertions to fallback_reason enum values.

Connor O’Brien (Release/SRE) — Comment:
- “Can we gate this under the standard integration step, not nightly? We need this signal pre-beta.”
Leila Farouk — Updated:
- Moved to the default Buildkite pipeline integration step (non-nightly) with a ~3m runtime.
